subject: claurst
title: clean-room claim unsupported: spec generated from the leaked Claude Code sourcemap, implementation comments port TS modules 1:1
evidence: README.md:208-218 (blog 'Claude Code's Entire Source Code Got Leaked via a Sourcemap in npm' as the origin) vs README.md:210 'clean-room'; spec/00_overview.md:3-8 (proprietary tree with per-file LOC); query/src/compact.rs:314 'Compaction prompt (matches TypeScript prompt.ts)'; core/src/memdir.rs:3-6 (four TS modules mapped); ~134 TS-mirroring comments
one_why: Same-owner analyze-leaked-then-implement pipeline has no clean-team firewall, and the 27k-LOC spec catalogues proprietary internals - derivative-work lineage like claw-code-agent, not the Phoenix v IBM posture the README invokes; concepts-only, no code-adjacent portables, and census provenance should not count it as a fork.

subject: claurst
title: documented stealth stack spoofs Claude Code client so subscription OAuth tokens pass Anthropic's gates
evidence: core/src/oauth_config.rs:51 ('stealth-impersonation constants'), :109 (extracted proprietary billing salt 59cf53e54c78), :113-124 (reconstructed cc_version client hash), :139 (verbatim system-prompt prefix), :170-190 (client-id purpose + live-verified quota-draw note); api/src/lib.rs:595-656 (apply_oauth_stealth strips own attribution, injects billing+identity blocks), :658 (wreq/BoringSSL chosen because 'TLS fingerprint matches Bun')
one_why: Deliberate provider-gate evasion (ToS/anti-circumvention exposure) that also disproves the clean-room claim - a salt lifted from the official bundle and a spoofed TLS fingerprint are not behavior-reimplementation; zero portables, and any adoption of this repo inherits takedown risk.

subject: claurst
title: /sandbox-toggle promises isolated shell execution; the setting is read by nothing but its own status display
evidence: commands/src/sandbox.rs:18-30 ('shell commands run in an isolated environment'), :44,:123,:137 (writes ui.sandbox_mode); grep sandbox_mode across src-rust: zero hits outside commands/; bash spawns via plain Command::new('bash')/PTY at tools/src/pty_bash.rs:163-181,393
one_why: Users who enable the toggle believe they have the crush/pi-tier 'nothing underneath' even removed - approval plus a fake kernel boundary is worse than honest absence (codel-2 'misleadingly reads' rung), and it caps safety-enforcement below the 6 anchor.

subject: claurst
title: repo-shipped .claurst/settings.json can inject shell hooks and permission rules while sibling fields are explicitly protected
evidence: core/src/lib.rs:1962 (hooks: merge_map(base, project-over)), :2005 (permission_rules extended by project file), :3986 (hooks run via sh -c on PreToolUse/Stop/UserPromptSubmit) vs :1992-2003 SECURITY comments blocking the same attack class for trust_project_mcp_servers, skip_dangerous_mode_permission_prompt, allowed_bash_prefixes
one_why: Cloning a hostile repo then opening claurst yields arbitrary code execution via hooks or pre-allowed tool rules; the codebase demonstrates it understands this exact vector three lines away - deny-by-default for code-execution-bearing fields must be uniform across the settings merge.

subject: claurst
title: project-MCP trust: fingerprint-keyed allowlist stored outside the repo, project settings barred from granting themselves trust
evidence: core/src/mcp_trust.rs:1-27 ('a repo can never grant itself trust'; user/project origin split, per-server launch-identity fingerprint in ~/.claurst/mcp_trust.json); core/src/lib.rs:1992-1997 (merge hard-blocks project trustProjectMcpServers); test at core/src/lib.rs:4649+ (origin tagging enforced)
one_why: Cleanest trust-gate found in the corpus for repo-defined executable surfaces - the three-part pattern (origin tag on load, out-of-repo persistent store keyed by fingerprint, settings-merge prohibition on self-grant) is the concept to copy; ironically claurst itself fails to apply it to hooks (claurst-4).

subject: claurst
title: central permission backstop with self-gates opt-out, secure-by-default for forgetful tools, contract pinned by tests
evidence: query/src/runner/tools.rs:65-72 (execute_tool gates any !self_gates tool at a gated level before execute); tools/src/lib.rs:520-532 (self_gates trait doc: 'a tool that forgets to call ctx.check_permission is still caught'); tests query/src/lib.rs:2504-2600 (denied tool must never run / no double-prompt / read-only exempt)
one_why: Inverts the usual failure mode: forgetting to gate a tool is caught by the executor rather than by reviewer diligence, and the three-way contract is an executable test - the loop-chokepoint design other harnesses should replicate (enforcement quality still bounded by rules being tool-name/glob only, no arg semantics for Bash).

subject: claurst
title: usage-truthed two-tier compaction with failure circuit-breaker and a files-touched manifest surviving cascaded compactions
evidence: query/src/compact.rs:891-899 (prefers last real provider usage over char/4, citing cache-read undercount), :44+267 (90% auto tier, 75% micro tier), :57-86 (breaker opens after 3 summarizer failures), :566-751 ('Files touched:' manifest parsed out of old summaries and re-merged into new ones), :1138-1164 (split snaps to tool_use/result pairing)
one_why: Two ideas worth copying: measuring the trigger against what the model actually received (pi's estimator, ported with the reasoning), and making compaction idempotent-with-memory by carrying a structured file manifest across successive summaries so multi-compaction sessions do not lose edit context.

subject: claurst
title: cache_control fully modeled on every request type but never set - prompt caching is never enabled on any provider
evidence: api/src/lib.rs:250-262 (CacheControl::ephemeral defined), :604 (cache_control: None); grep 'CacheControl::ephemeral' across all 294 .rs files: 0 construction sites
one_why: Every turn re-bills the full context on a harness that otherwise measures usage truthfully and compacts at 90% - the compaction machinery exists precisely because costs balloon, yet the one mechanism that would slash steady-state input cost is dead code; cautionary pairing for token-economy scoring.

subject: claurst
title: /goal multi-turn objectives with budget guards plus 'ultracode' keyword that swaps top effort AND injects a plan-delegate-integrate-verify fanout procedure
evidence: core/src/effort.rs:273-405 (ULTRACODE_KEYWORD, ULTRACODE_PROCEDURE), core/src/keywords.rs:72,103 (word-boundary matching); query/src/goal_loop.rs:79-99 (decide_goal_continuation with Complete/Paused/BudgetLimited stops); query/src/lib.rs:640-647 (per-turn effort override)
one_why: No other corpus subject composes an in-prompt keyword escalation with a bounded multi-turn objective policy - the continuation_policy consulted at every end_turn (:436-441) is a clean seam; distinct from goal-movies-style infinite loops because guards are code, not prompt.
